description:
From the fz-kdt.186 cold review (2026-09-03). Once the seat asks
reachability first (Seating::Separated: no value satisfies both arms'
conjunctions), a separated pair is left as it arrived -- correctly, since no
routing depends on it. But fz-kdt.186's fiction was accidentally PINNING a
schedule-free order on such pairs: on 00420_enum_take_drop_split and
behavior/enum_take_drop_split the call-edge plan cs0 inside
List.reduce_while_cont/3 clause 1 (s1 {:cont, ..} vs {:cont | :halt, ..}, s2
two disjoint closure-literal sets) was moved to a seat by a containment at s1
that the disjoint s2 made irrelevant; with the truthful rule it keeps arrival.
Measured under FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH=arms:3: canon differs from the
settled canon on 23 fixtures at base and 25 after 186 -- the two extras are
exactly those two.
CONCORDANCE: fz-kdt.107 (closed) owns the INSEPARABLE class (one question,
a value reaches both members: order decides meaning, so no canonical order is
allowed); fz-kdt.131 (open) owns overlap-without-containment (a value reaches
both, neither surface covers: order decides representation safety). This
ticket is the third, SAFE class: no value reaches both, so a canonical
tie-break (cmp_tys over the arms' observable surfaces, the fz-kdt.101/105/108
key) changes no routing and removes the axis. Cure: in specificity_order,
after the covering pass, order Separated-only neighbours canonically -- and
prove it changes no routing with the same first-match argument the 186
review gave (order changes a destination only for a value satisfying both
conjunctions). Red-first: the two fixtures' cs0 order invariant under every
arms: seed; the arms:3 artifact-mover count 25 -> 23 or lower. State in
specificity_order's doc which of the three residues each pair class is.
title: A SEPARATED arm pair keeps arrival order: meaning-free by construction, but one more artifact axis a schedule can move -- a canonical tie-break is provably safe exactly there
